Cybersecurity: 16 major news items from September 13, 2026 (including Cyber Resilience Act)

DCOD cybersecurity digest covering the week's key developments:

Key events: ENISA launched the first stage of the Single Reporting Platform (SRP) under the Cyber Resilience Act, an online tool for one-time reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities and serious incidents. In Berlin, after refusing to pay a 30-Bitcoin ransom, the Rhysida ransomware group published nearly 6 terabytes of data on the dark web, affecting approximately 1.44 million files and 12,076 individuals. On September 6, Liquid Network (Bitcoin sidechain) was drained of approximately 4,000 bitcoins from a federation wallet; 3,400 were later returned while roughly 598 were retained. Microsoft published its largest-ever Patch Tuesday (September 2026) with up to 974 vulnerabilities patched, including 2 already exploited, 20 wormable vulnerabilities, and remote code execution on Exchange via a Visio attachment.

Additional coverage: IDScan confirmed a data breach with over 150 million driver's licenses stolen. A threat actor generated 1 million personalized fraudulent emails in 3 days using AI. Cloudflare added post-quantum DNSSEC support to its 1.1.1.1 resolver. Germany expressed concern about replacing American Palantir dependency with a French alternative. Anthropic reported Chinese and Russian actors weaponizing its AI for drones, surveillance, and biological weapons. Russian developers allegedly used AI to build kamikaze attack drone software for Ukraine. Four nation-state actors used the same Chrome zero-day exploit kit (BlueMoon) within 12 days. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an AI slowdown. The EU quantum act will not have a dedicated budget. ETH Zurich will host a new IBM quantum computer. The FBI released a new cyber strategy emphasizing faster operations and greater industry role. Switzerland's federal government is testing open-source alternatives to Microsoft on 3,000 computers.

via Mastodon https://dcod.ch/2026/09/13/cybersecurite-16-actualites-majeures-du-13-septembre-2026-dont-cyber-resilience-act/
